00:00 🖥️ AI infrastructure investments.
- The world's impending need to invest in infrastructure for AI at larger scales.

- Criticism of Sam Altman for fundraising outside OpenAI and his response clarifying the misrepresentation.

comments.text:
4:43 to help out and make it simpler:

Traditional silicon chips have transistors / logic gates that are either open or closed in the circuit to represent a 0 or a 1. Each chip has billions of these.

Neuromorphic is silicon designed to mimic a brain with its neurons and structures represented and printed on silicon. 

The analog vs digital bit is the way the chip operates: neuromorphic chips calculate a result by running electricity to produce a result without being controlled by software, it’s a hardware medium. 
Digital signal software controlled, each transistor has binary state that contributes to the compute operation. 
Digital is a slow conversation between hardware and software and analog is an instant (close to instant) computation done only on hardware.

comments.text: Great channel, and I think 99% of the info here is legit. However in this case I don't think the description of a neuromorphic is quite right. The gate activations still represent "1"s and "0"s however the architecture is not Von Neumann. The memory and compute are one in the same in neuromorphic chips since the structure itself represents the weights and biases of the neural net rather than representation in a matrix  that has to be shuffled back abd forth between the CPU and RAM.
